feature.title: 公開 API 仕様の取得とオフライン生成
flow: User and player OpenApiRouter registrations produce offline documents and their anonymous /openapi.json responses.
The gateway exports a separate offline matchmaking OpenAPI document with owner-scoped routes and cookie alternatives.
Example binaries serialize these library documents; document generation does not start the services.

guarantees.statement: User and player expose anonymous /openapi.json equal to offline generation without repository access or user identity-provider calls.
Player OpenAPI identifies its service and describes its routes, query/error contracts and public response schemas.
User OpenAPI identifies its service and describes its routes, cookie alternatives, DTOs, error media and redirect headers.
The gateway offline document includes the five owner-scoped matchmaking operations and production/development session-cookie alternatives.
The three example commands print library OpenAPI JSON without requiring service startup.

contracts.statement: The player document route returns the same generated OpenAPI as player_http::openapi without reading storage.

evidence.reason: Anonymous router response equals offline JSON and panic-on-use record/rating repositories remain untouched.

contracts.statement: Player route-derived OpenAPI 3.1 has package identity, exact method/path set, query/error constraints and public response shapes.

evidence.reason: Package name/version are checked, with absent dependency-derived contact/license.
OpenAPI 3.1, exact four paths and methods, parameter constraints, enumerated errors and resolvable local refs are asserted.
Assertions compare flattened actions, required nullable cursor and unsigned integer bounds with actual DTO JSON.

contracts.statement: The user document route returns offline OpenAPI without storage or identity-provider calls and applies private response headers.

evidence.reason: HTTPS and development in-process routers return equal offline JSON with security headers; repository and provider panic if used.

contracts.statement: User route-derived OpenAPI has service identity, the exact six operations, cookie security alternatives and request/response schemas.

evidence.reason: Package name/version are checked, without contact/license attribution from dependencies.
Exact paths/methods, cookie alternatives, headers, redirects, DTO fields, error enums and all local references are asserted.
Runtime framework text rejections and application JSON rejections are checked against documented status/media and no-store.
The documented PATCH response status set, JSON ErrorBody references, framework text schemas and callback text rejection are compared directly.

contracts.gap: The runtime rejection sample does not cover every response family or all success/error headers. The schema checks do not establish provider availability.

contracts.statement: The gateway exports annotated matchmaking paths and two cookie security schemes through its offline OpenAPI accessor.

evidence.reason: The generated document contains GET /matchmaking/me, GET/PUT/DELETE ticket and POST heartbeat operations plus both cookie names and OR security alternatives.

contracts.gap: This test checks presence rather than exact equality of the gateway method/path set. The completeness catalog separately reconciles generated operations. Gateway has no runtime /openapi.json route.

contracts.statement: The player, user and matchmaking example entrypoints serialize their library document as pretty JSON.
contracts.gap: No mapped test launches the example processes or checks their stdout, the shell generation script or published files. Equivalent examples are crates/user-http/examples/user-openapi.rs and crates/realtime-gateway/examples/matchmaking-openapi.rs.

limitations: Generated schema assertions and in-process responses do not prove documentation publication or real example-command stdout.
Only user and player have runtime document endpoints. The gateway document covers matchmaking; the WebSocket protocol is outside that OpenAPI.
Source links and successful test execution establish traceable evidence, not semantic proof or complete coverage of these guarantees.
